text.p: Following are the top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- A South Korean jumbo jet crashed on Guam, killing 224 passengers and crew but 30 survived, including some who walked away from the burning wreckage.
- Cambodia's National Assembly voted in Ung Huot as First Prime Minister to replace ousted Prince Norodom Ranariddh and stripped the prince of his legal immunity.

- A record number of 215 people were struck down by dengue fever in one week last month, spurring town councils to put their heads together to find ways of tackling this serious threat to Singaporeans' health.
- About S$14 million in Central Provident Fund savings were lost through insurance policies surrendered, cancelled or which had lapsed in the three-and-a-half years to June.

- Market perception that the Government did an about-turn when it opted to license more basic telephone operators from 2002 is "unwarranted", Communications Minister Mah Bow Tan said. - Response to the state land tender for two industrial sites showed a general weakening in the market segment with lower bids from fewer developers.
- Company performance was down sharply in the second quarter, with only foreign-owned firms emerging unscathed, a survey by BT and the Centre for Business Research & Development at NUS has found.

- In a measure intended to boost the stock market, the Malaysian government has pushed through a bill that will allow companies to buy back their own shares or offer financial aid to third parties to buy their stock.

- Apple Computer and Microsoft stunned the computer industry with a tie-up that will see Microsoft buying a S$220 million stake in Apple and the sharing of technology by two of the fiercest rivals in the industry.

- DBS Bank posted a healthy 13 percent rise in group net profit to S$358.3 million for the first half-year on the back of strong loans growth despite a slow-down in the economy and turmoil in the regional markets.
- The suspension of finance company Sri Dhana will actually facilitate DBS Bank's process of acquiring a majority stake in it, DBS Bank president Ng Kee Choe said.
- OCBC Bank is bearish about economic recovery in the second half and has told analysts that domestic loans growth could, in a worst-case scenario, fall to single-digit levels.
- Hotel Properties Ltd reported a 24.5 percent rise in net profit to S$13.3 million for the half year ended June 30.
